title: Subtraction inside a signed finite sum over the constructed integers
statement: `Int.sumRange (fun k => f k - g k) n = Int.sumRange f n - Int.sumRange g n`. WHY IT IS THE POINT: ADR-1260 measured that Eisenstein's lemma routes around the missing-aggregate wall but needs subtraction inside a finite sum, and the Int prelude folded PRODUCTS only -- `Int.prodRange` with 132 rows against zero `Int.sumRange` rows, because Wilson's theorem and Euler's totient theorem both multiply. HOW IT IS PROVED: no induction at all. `Int.sub a b := add a (neg b)` is a plain non-recursive `Definition`, so the stated left-hand side is definitionally `Int.sumRange_add` instantiated at `g := fun k => -(g k)`, and one congruence through `Int.sumRange_neg` finishes it. `Int.prodRange` has no analogue because the integers have no multiplicative inverse to fold. `Kernel::axiom_footprint` is EMPTY. Admitted by the trusted gate on the first attempt.

formal.statement: theorem Int.sumRange_sub : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Int)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Int)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.sumRange (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Int.sub (x0 x3) (x1 x3)) x2) (Int.sub (Int.sumRange x0 x2) (Int.sumRange x1 x2)))))
